evaluation_target.rationale: The safety goal explicitly states that the system shall prevent omitting required braking maneuvers, and the hazard describes omission of braking as the hazardous event leading to collision.

phenomenon_of_interest.statement: The vehicle’s braking-relevant response to obstacle/collision-avoidance situations.
phenomenon_of_interest.scope: Situations in which the system is driving and must decide whether to initiate a braking maneuver to avoid collision with an obstacle or road user, including obstacle-detection and control situations referenced by the provided requirements and hazard.
phenomenon_of_interest.rationale: The concern is about omitted braking in collision-avoidance contexts, so the relevant phenomenon is the braking response in those situations rather than any specific sensor or controller implementation.

distinctions.dimension: Braking response in a collision-avoidance situation
distinctions.contrast_a: A required braking maneuver is initiated in time to avoid collision
distinctions.contrast_b: A required braking maneuver is omitted or not initiated in time
distinctions.rationale: The hazard distinguishes the presence versus omission of braking, and FR-7/FR-7.1 indicate that braking must occur after obstacle detection to avoid collisions. Collapsing these would remove exactly the information needed to evaluate whether braking omission occurs.

distinctions.dimension: Obstacle detection status relevant to braking decision
distinctions.contrast_a: An obstacle is detected within the relevant dangerous zone / in time for braking
distinctions.contrast_b: An obstacle is not detected, or not detected in time, for braking to be triggered
distinctions.rationale: FR-7.1 and FR-7.2.5 require timely obstacle detection within the dangerous zone, and FR-7.2/FR-7.2.1 require obstacle detection. Collapsing detected-versus-not-detected/too-late situations would lose information needed to judge whether an omitted braking maneuver is attributable to missed detection.

distinctions.dimension: Brake-actuator availability for executing a commanded braking maneuver
distinctions.contrast_a: Brake actuators are functioning sufficiently to execute braking
distinctions.contrast_b: Brake actuators have failed and cannot execute braking as commanded
distinctions.rationale: SR-1.5 and SR-1.6 require identification and mitigation of brake actuator failures. If these situations were indistinguishable, the representation could not support evaluation of whether braking omission is due to actuator failure rather than a missing braking command.

orrs.obligation: An admissible Observable Representation shall preserve whether a braking maneuver required for collision avoidance was initiated versus omitted/not initiated in time.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must distinguish states in which the required braking maneuver occurs in time from states in which it does not occur or occurs too late.

orrs.obligation: An admissible Observable Representation shall preserve whether obstacle detection relevant to the braking decision occurred in time for braking to be triggered.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must distinguish obstacle-detected-in-time states from obstacle-not-detected or detected-too-late states.

orrs.obligation: An admissible Observable Representation shall preserve whether brake actuator failure is present when evaluating omission of braking.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must distinguish functioning brake-actuator states from brake-actuator-failed states.
